Nobody has ever told me "I love having my picture taken."

Twenty years in and I've heard the opposite a thousand times — I'm not photogenic, I hate my smile, can you fix my neck.

Here's what I've learned: it's almost never about the face. It's that most people have never been photographed by someone who was paying attention.

Twenty minutes of somebody actually looking at you, and you find out you were photogenic the whole time.

#headshots #personalbranding #professionalphotography

Your LinkedIn photo is doing one of two jobs right now.

It's either telling people you're the kind of professional they want to work with — or it's quietly asking them to overlook it.

There's no third option. There's no neutral photo. The cropped wedding picture from 2019 is making an argument about you whether you meant it to or not.

#linkedintips #personalbrand #headshots

What a headshot day actually looks like from my side.

Fifty people. One room. Eight hours. Two lights and a laptop.

Everybody walks in apologizing for something — their hair, their weight, the fact that they "don't do pictures." Everybody walks out standing a little straighter.

That's the whole job. The camera is almost beside the point.

#behindthescenes #headshots #eventphotography

Twenty minutes.

That's how long a headshot session takes at one of our events. Most people spend longer than that picking which old photo to crop.

The difference between the two is about four years of looking like you haven't updated anything.

#headshots #professionalheadshots #personalbranding

A client asked me last month whether he should "tone it down" for his headshot. Lose the hat. Wear something more corporate.

I told him no.

If the photo doesn't look like you, it's not working for you — it's working for some idea of what a professional is supposed to look like. And that idea has never closed a deal in its life.

Come as the person your clients actually meet.

#personalbrand #authenticity #headshots

Seventy-five dollars. Twenty minutes. A photo you'll use for the next three years.

We run headshot events around Central Florida — one room, professional lighting, and you walk out with images that same week.

It's the least expensive thing we do and the one most people meet us through.

The most common thing I fix isn't lighting. It's posture.

People shrink in front of a camera. Shoulders forward, chin down, bracing for it.

Half of what I do in a session is get somebody to stop bracing. You can see the exact frame where it happens — and that's almost always the one they pick.

#photography #headshots #bodylanguage

Two lights, a backdrop, and a folding table.

People assume the gear is the thing. It isn't. I've shot headshots in conference rooms, church fellowship halls, a car dealership showroom and somebody's living room.

What the room can't give you is the twenty minutes of attention. That part travels with me.

#behindthescenes #photography #smallbusiness

"Can you make me look like I did ten years ago?"

No. And I wouldn't if I could.

The goal was never to look younger. It's to look like the best version of who you are right now — which is the version your clients are actually going to meet.

Every time somebody sees the photo before they see you, the photo should be making a promise you can keep.

#headshots #personalbranding #authenticity

A headshot has a shelf life. Most people don't realize it's about three years.

Not because you've changed that much — because the photo starts to feel like a different era. The lighting, the crop, the background, the way you styled your hair.

If your photo is older than your current job title, it's working against the story you're telling.

#linkedintips #personalbrand #professionalphotography

Something I've noticed after years of this.

A good headshot fixes the first impression. It doesn't fix what happens next — the website that doesn't sound like you, the follow-up that never went out, the inquiry that sat until Monday.

That gap is the reason our photography studio turned into a branding and marketing agency. People kept coming for the photo and staying for the rest of it.

If the photo is the only part that's working, that's worth a conversation.

#personalbrand #smallbusiness #branding

If your headshot is older than three years, this is your sign.
